fields.paraphrase: Pārvatī asks why Nala performed the vow. Himavat describes Niṣadha’s king as Veda-knowing, brave, generous, wealthy and pure, skilled with chariot, sword, arrows, bow, quiver and armour, and able to travel the three worlds. His innumerable cavalry, elephants, chariots, bowmen and weapon/fire-weapon fighters frighten Indra and direction-lords. His wife Damayantī is beautiful, virtuous and adorned; Brahmā fashioned her from selected essence and gave her the beauty of women in the three worlds. Minister Padmahasta is valiant, intelligent like Bṛhaspati, skilled in policy like Aṅgiras.

fields.paraphrase: Padmahasta is compared to Meru in height and the ocean in depth. A court with Apsaras dancers, praisers and brahmarṣis receives Gautama. Nala honours and seats him, calling his own birth, kingship, parents, lineage and life fruitful through the visit. Gautama says he wanted to see the king’s wealth, reports praise by Brahmā, Indra, Hari and Śiva, then asks leave. Nala pleads that he stay to remove uncertainty; the sage agrees. The king asks which merit or tapas produced his extraordinary wealth and who he was in a former birth.
